title: Agent Stream Event (v12)
description: SSE frame payload for GET /api/v2/chat/stream. v3 added tool_call and tool_result event types for evidence panel rendering (SPEC-011 R-1). v4 adds confirmation_request and confirmation_result event types for HITL confirmation bridging (SPEC-020 R-1). v5 adds an optional data field on tool_result frames carrying the full tool payload within the stream size cap. v6 adds an optional risk_level on each pending_calls entry so confirmation cards can surface mutating (write/admin) tool calls (SPEC-021 R-3). v7 adds an optional model field on message_end frames carrying the model id that resolved for the turn (SPEC-024 R-3/R-4). v8 adds an optional action on each pending_calls entry carrying the policy action derived from the risk tier so the tiered require_approval confirmation bridge and portal approval badges can render (SPEC-030 R-3). v9 adds an optional flow_summary on confirmation_request frames carrying the bound browser-flow headline so the live operator card renders the same workflow framing the durable record gives the approver inbox (SPEC-051 R-6). v10 adds an optional flow_intent inside flow_summary carrying the skill-authored sentence describing what the flow's gated mutating step achieves, rendered as the card's lead decision line (SPEC-053 R-2) — shipped at 0.34.0 but never recorded in this title/ledger, retro-fitted here. v11 adds an optional approval_kind on confirmation_request frames declaring whether the parked batch is a bound browser flow or an individually-approved action, so a card's kind is stated rather than inferred from ambient session state (SPEC-054 R-1), plus an optional display-only change_request projection on each pending_calls entry so an action card reads as a secret-masked change request instead of a bare tool name (SPEC-054 R-3). v11 also declares display_hint, which SPEC-050 already emits on pending_calls entries but never added to this schema (additionalProperties is false, so the omission was a latent contract violation). v12 adds a secret_delivery event type (SPEC-062 R-3): a dedicated frame emitted as a sibling of tool_result when a secrets.generate_password result carries a delivery_id, so the portal can render a one-time Copy-password control. It carries delivery_id, channel, expires_at and an optional recipient — never the generated value, which rides no projection at all (the frame is a handle to a server-mediated single-use redemption, ADR-0012). A dedicated frame rather than a field on tool_result.data keeps the contract stable independent of the data size-cap omission and is self-describing to the portal; older clients ignore the unknown type.

delta.description: Incremental text chunk. Present on message_delta frames.

message.description: Terminal metadata. Present on message_end and error frames. Carries the kernel permission message on confirmation_request frames.

model.description: Model id that resolved for the turn (SPEC-024 R-3/R-4). Present on message_end frames so downstream tees can attribute the turn.

confirm_id.description: Unique identifier correlating a confirmation_request with its confirmation_result and the confirm endpoint call. Present on confirmation_request and confirmation_result frames.

pending_calls.description: Batch of parked tool calls awaiting confirmation. Present on confirmation_request frames and echoed on the matching confirmation_result frame.

risk_level.description: Tool risk tier when known at park time (SPEC-021 R-3); absent for tools without a gateway risk tier.

action.description: Policy action the parked call maps to, derived from the risk tier at park time (SPEC-030 R-3): read -> tools:invoke, write/admin -> tools:mutate. Absent for tools without a gateway risk tier; the confirm bridge treats absent as the implicit no-rule path.

display_hint.description: SPEC-050: parsed browser-element label for a parked web.* write (e.g. "Reset password button"), rendered as the card's per-call hint. Display-only, never a security input and never part of args_digest. Emitted since 0.32.0; declared here at v11 to close a latent additionalProperties violation.

change_request.description: SPEC-054 R-3: display-only change-request projection for one parked call, promoting the decision-relevant parameters out of the collapsed technical-details expander into the approval intention. Assembled as a sibling of parameters, so args_digest (computed over parameters alone) and therefore the signature and gateway verification are unaffected by it. Secret-bearing values are masked to *** with the key preserved. Absent for tools without a projection and for clients predating v11, which render today's tool-level card.

summary.description: Short human sentence naming the target and the effect, e.g. 'Delete pod "scratch-restart-demo" in namespace "default"'. Rendered as the card's lead line.

fields.description: Optional label/value pairs rendered as a table beneath the summary. Omitted when the projection has nothing worth tabulating beyond the summary.

masked.description: True when the value was replaced by *** because it is secret-bearing (name-based masking) or sits on a per-tool opaque-value list such as web.type.text. The label is always preserved so the approver can see that a secret is involved without seeing it.

approval_kind.description: SPEC-054 R-1: declares what the parked batch is, on confirmation_request frames. "flow" means a bound browser web-check flow collapsing to one gate (SPEC-051); "action" means an individually-approved mutating tool call. Derived at park time from the parked batch itself — a browser write in the batch AND a bound flow context — never from ambient session state, which is the structural fix behind the v0.34.1 headline-leak patch. Display-driving only: the signed execution envelope carries its own approval_kind stamped by whichever builder signed it (ADR-0010), and the two agree whenever the kernel's flow view is current. Absent for clients predating v11, which fall back to today's tool-level rendering.

flow_summary.description: SPEC-051 R-6: card-level browser-flow headline on confirmation_request frames (skill intent, origin, risk_class) so the live operator card renders the same workflow framing as the durable record served to the approver inbox. SPEC-053 R-2 adds flow_intent: the skill-authored sentence describing what the flow's gated mutating step achieves, rendered as the card's lead decision line (display-only, never a security input). Absent for non-browser cards. SPEC-054 R-1: present if and only if approval_kind is "flow" — the kernel emits both from the same branch, so an action card can never inherit a lingering flow's headline.

tool_name.description: Name of the invoked tool. Present on tool_call and tool_result frames.

call_id.description: Unique identifier correlating a tool_call with its tool_result within a request.

parameters.description: LLM-supplied tool parameters. Present on tool_call frames.

status.description: Outcome marker. Present on tool_result frames (success/error/denied) and confirmation_result frames (approved/denied/expired/interrupted).

evidence.description: Execution provenance metadata. Present on tool_result frames.

data_summary.description: Condensed tool result for UI rendering (bounded size). Present on tool_result frames.

data.description: Full tool result payload when its serialized size stays within the stream cap (AGENT_TOOL_DATA_MAX_CHARS); omitted when oversized. Present on tool_result frames.

error.description: Error details. Present on error and failed tool_result frames.

delivery_id.description: SPEC-062 R-3: opaque single-use handle for a generated secret's redemption. Present on secret_delivery frames; the portal binds a Copy-password control to it and exchanges it once via the authenticated GET /api/v2/secrets/delivery/{id}. Never the value itself.

channel.description: SPEC-062 R-3/R-5: delivery channel the handle belongs to (portal_copy today; email and future channels are additive, so this is an open string, not a closed enum). Present on secret_delivery frames.

expires_at.description: SPEC-062 R-3: when the handle stops being redeemable (the buffer TTL). Present on secret_delivery frames so the portal can render an expired state without a round trip.

recipient.description: SPEC-062 R-4: the external recipient for a non-local channel (e.g. an email address). Present on secret_delivery frames for external channels; absent for portal_copy, whose recipient is the session owner.
